Subject: Production errors + 7-12x token volume spike this morning

Hi Karthik / Laura,

We started seeing a large increase in request volume to the Redwood endpoint around 07:40 PT this morning. Throughput jumped ~7x compared to baseline and error rate climbed to ~9% for ~20 minutes. This caused a visible impact on our user flows (login -> summary generation).

We need a short incident summary and immediate mitigation plan — our ops team has screenshots and a Kibana session they can share. Can you confirm:
- What caused the volume jump? (traffic vs retry storms)
- Any immediate fixes we can apply while you investigate?
- ETA for a post-incident RCA and timeline for corrective actions?

We’re available for a quick bridge now if helpful.

Thanks,
Maya Gomez
Site Reliability Lead, AzuraHealth

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production errors + 7-12x token volume spike this morning

Maya — thanks for flagging and sorry for the disruption. We spun up a bridge (link in separate email) and our on-call SREs are looking at logs. Initial ask: please share the Kibana session and any trace IDs you have so we can correlate.

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Temporarily increased request quota for your org (5m burst) to reduce client-side retries.
- Activated fallback routing to a lower-latency model variant for interactive endpoints (no change to your config required).

Rishi is leading the investigation; I’ve looped in Laura and Jonas given potential executive impact. We’ll keep updates on the bridge and deliver a draft RCA by EOD tomorrow.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Rishi: initial root-cause hypotheses + log excerpts (ETA 2h)
- Karthik: customer comms / credits options (ETA 4h)
- Laura / Jonas: exec notification + any contractual decisions (as needed)

— Karthik

On Thu, Oct 7, 2027 at 09:12 Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Maya — thanks for flagging and sorry for the disruption.

Team — quick summary from initial triage:
- Timeline: 07:38 PT — sudden request-rate surge originating from two Azura ingestion endpoints (IDs: azura-ingest-1, azura-ingest-2). 07:40–07:58 PT — concurrent queue growth on the inference pool serving gen-large models; 07:40–08:02 PT — spike of 4xx/5xx errors (predominantly 503s), peak error-rate ~9%.
- Probable cause: combination of a misconfigured retry backoff on Azura’s client ingestion (duplicate replays during an upstream delay) and a regression in our batching backpressure logic for sequences >4k tokens under sudden fanout.
- Evidence: attached token_usage_spike_20271007.csv (sampled per-minute token counts), and a truncated log excerpt included below. Full logs uploaded to shared drive.

Log excerpt (truncated):
[2027-10-07T07:40:02Z] pool=gen-large queue=238 latency_p95=820ms errors=0.32%
[2027-10-07T07:45:11Z] pool=gen-large queue=1249 latency_p95=1540ms errors=3.7%
[2027-10-07T07:50:07Z] pool=gen-large queue=3120 latency_p95=2.1s errors=9.1%

Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Dynamic per-org burst throttling (reduced retries) — decreased retry amplification.
- Forced model-variant fallback for Azura interactive endpoints.
- Short-term autoscale buffer increase for gen-large pool (manual).

Follow-up plan (owner / ETA):
1) Full RCA (Rishi) — include sequence-length distribution, batching behavior, and kernel selection trace. ETA: 48 hours (draft).
2) Runtime fix (Infra) — patch batching backpressure for long sequences; will be scoped as a high-priority patch. ETA: 5 business days for rollout to staging, 10 business days to production (with canary).
3) Customer guidance (Karthik + Laura) — recommend client retry/backoff changes and token-cost controls. ETA: customer-facing doc + sample config tomorrow.
4) Credits/contract relief (Laura + Jonas) — recommend a one-off usage credit for impacted window; discuss SLA implications. ETA: same-day exec decision.

Attachments: token_usage_spike_20271007.csv; uploaded full logs to https://drive.redwood.ai/azura/logs/20271007

— Rishi
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: AzuraHealth incident — mitigation plan and exec asks

Jonas / Grace — quick readout and requested decisions:

Summary: customer saw a transient throughput and error-rate surge on Oct 7; initial triage points to retry amplification plus a batching backpressure regression. Rishi has a scoped remediation but it will take ~10 business days to fully roll out to production.

Requested executive decisions (today):
1) Approve a one-off credit of up to $18k (we absorbed their excess token usage during the impacted window). This is customer goodwill to preserve renewal momentum.
2) Commit to a formal post-incident review — cross-functional stakeholders (SRE, Runtime, Product) to present final RCA and remediation validation within 14 days.
3) Approve priority tagging for the runtime backpressure patch (we will allocate an infra patch slot).

Proposed customer-facing deliverables (for Azura):
- 48-hour draft RCA (Rishi) — shareable with Azura ops.
- Short-term configuration guide to avoid retry storms + sample client backoff (Karthik) — publish tomorrow.
- Formal post-incident RCA + validation report (cross-functional) — 14 days.

I recommend we route the credit approval and formal review commit via Jonas since this touches SLA. If approved, I will send the formal reconciliation and credit memo to Maya.

— Laura
